title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #127 review (frontend-stock-detail-metric-help)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #127 (frontend-stock-detail-metric-help), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. None of these blocked the PR on their own -- the review's blocking finding (an inaccurate Trigger current-value interpretation) is tracked directly on the parent task instead, since it sent that PR back to implementing.

checklist.step: common/MetricHelp's trigger uses a hardcoded static `data-testid="metric-help-icon"`, but MetricHelp is instantiated ~16 times on a single StockDetailPage render (5 in IndicatorsPanel, 4 in ScreensPanel, up to 7 in SignalSummary including per-breakdown-row). A future test querying `getByTestId('metric-help-icon')` to target one specific metric's icon will hit a 'multiple elements found' (vitest/Testing Library) or Playwright strict-mode violation, or silently grab the wrong instance. Drop the testid (the unique `triggerAriaLabel`-derived aria-label already supports querying by accessible name/role) or derive it per-instance (e.g. via `useId()`, the same pattern InfoBalloon already uses for its own `popoverId`).

No call-site-level tests were added for SignalSummary.tsx/ScreensPanel.tsx/IndicatorsPanel.tsx confirming the right MetricHelp opens with the right content when wired with real component props (checklist item 6 on the parent task claims this done). Only common/MetricHelp itself (MetricHelp.test.tsx) and the content registry's interpretValue functions (metricHelpContent.test.ts) are directly unit-tested; the three panel components reach 100% coverage only via pre-existing renders that happen to mount the new MetricHelp instances, not via a new test that clicks a wired icon and asserts the right metric's content appears. Add at least one such test per panel (e.g. click the EMA13 corner icon in IndicatorsPanel and assert the EMA13-specific text renders, not a different metric's).

tideHelp.interpretValue's Neutral-case message (metricHelpContent.ts) unconditionally states 'the weekly slope and EMA13/26 relationship disagree', but per backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py's evaluate_tide, NEUTRAL can also arise from a genuinely flat/ambiguous slope alone (not necessarily the slope actively disagreeing with the EMA relationship) -- the same family of inaccuracy as the blocking Trigger finding on the parent task, but much lower-impact since the dynamic slope label ('flat') is still shown alongside it. Tighten the wording to cover the flat-slope case accurately (e.g. branch on `weekly_macd_histogram_slope === 'flat'` the same way triggerHelp will need to branch on tide after its fix).

[Found in PR #127 round-2 re-review] tideHelp.interpretValue's now-fixed 'genuinely flat' branch (metricHelpContent.ts, added to resolve the item above) is itself inaccurate for evaluate_tide's <2-weekly-bar short-circuit (backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py, `if len(weekly_ohlcv) < 2: return TideResult(trend="NEUTRAL", weekly_macd_histogram_slope="flat")`), which never computes a slope at all -- the message claims 'the weekly MACD-H slope is genuinely flat, so there's no clear direction to read' when in fact no reading was ever taken. Same class of two-distinct-causes conflation as the original blocking Trigger finding, but narrower (requires <2 weekly bars, unreachable by any current fixture ticker). Branch the message on bar count too (or otherwise distinguish 'flat reading' from 'no reading possible yet'), mirroring triggerHelp's own tideTrend-based branch.

[Found in PR #127 round-2 re-review] signalExplanation.ts's HOLD-explanation headline for a Neutral tide (the 'Why HOLD?' balloon from the merged frontend-signal-why-explanation PR #125, not touched by PR #127) unconditionally states 'the weekly MACD-Histogram slope and the 13/26-week EMA relationship disagree', the identical inaccuracy metricHelpContent.ts's tideHelp.interpretValue just had fixed in PR #127 -- left uncorrected in this second, adjacent call site on the same StockDetailPage. For a flat-slope Neutral ticker this now visibly contradicts the freshly-corrected tideHelp balloon right next to it. Apply the same flat-vs-disagree (and, per the item above, flat-vs-insufficient-history) branching here.

decisions.decision: All three checklist items here were addressed directly on the parent task's needs_work fix-up pass (PR #127), rather than as a separate follow-up PR, since they landed in the same files already being touched for the blocking Trigger fix. See frontend-stock-detail-metric-help.json's own `decisions` array for the specifics of each fix.
decisions.rationale: Deferring these to a later, separate PR would have meant a second review pass over the same three files (MetricHelp.tsx, metricHelpContent.ts, and the three panel test files) for changes that were already low-risk and in scope while PR #127 was open for the blocking fix; bundling them avoided that duplicate review cost. Left this task's own state as `planned` (not moved to `done`) since a follow-up task's `done` state should be set by whoever re-reviews/QAs the resolution, consistent with how `review`/`test` fields elsewhere on the board are written by the reviewing agent rather than the implementing one.

decisions.decision: Fixed both remaining checklist items by naming both candidate causes ('there isn't enough weekly price history yet to compute a slope, or the weekly MACD-H slope is genuinely flat') in the flat-slope Neutral-Tide message, rather than actually branching on weekly bar count as the checklist's primary suggestion phrased it -- confirmed via `backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py`'s `evaluate_tide` directly (0-bar, 1-bar, and a 30-identical-close-bar genuinely-flat-slope case all return the exact same `TideResult(trend='NEUTRAL', weekly_macd_histogram_slope='flat')`) that the two causes are indistinguishable from the API response alone: `TideScreen` (backend/app/api/schemas.py) exposes only `trend`/`weekly_macd_histogram_slope`, no weekly bar count, and neither `ScreensPanel.tsx`/`tideHelp.interpretValue` nor `signalExplanation.ts`'s `explainSignal` receive the raw weekly OHLCV or any other discriminating signal. Applied the identical fix to signalExplanation.ts's HOLD-headline-adjacent tide condition `detail` (the actual site of the 'disagree' text the checklist calls the 'headline' -- `explanation.headline` itself never said 'disagree'; the Neutral-tide `tide` condition's `detail`, rendered directly under the headline in the same balloon, is what did), branching on `screens.tide.weekly_macd_histogram_slope` the same way.
decisions.rationale: The checklist's suggested fix (mirror triggerHelp's tideTrend-based branch) doesn't transfer directly: triggerHelp could disambiguate its own 'not_applicable' two-cause overlap because `tideTrend` is a *second, independently exposed* field it already receives that happens to pin down which cause applies. Tide's own NEUTRAL/'flat' overlap has no such second field -- both causes collapse to the identical `(trend, slope)` pair with nothing else in `TideScreen` to tell them apart, so 'branch on bar count' would require a new API field (out of scope for a frontend-only follow-up, and the checklist itself notes this case is 'unreachable by any current fixture ticker', i.e. too low-impact to justify a dedicated backend task the way the analogous Wave-lookback gap was -- api-stocks-analysis-wave-lookback). Naming both possibilities without asserting either fixes the actual inaccuracy (no longer claims a specific, possibly-wrong cause) using only data already available, at the cost of a slightly less specific message for this narrow edge case -- accepted as the right tradeoff over adding backend plumbing for a case no current ticker reaches.
